chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdul Kareem, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'Inform me about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And for the divorced women a provision with the goodness; this is a right upon the pious.' What is the lowest of that provision when he is financially tight, he cannot find it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'A scarf or something resembling it.'

key_terms.بِالْمَعْرُوفِ: With goodness or in a fair manner
key_terms.مَتَاعٌ: Provision or gift given to a divorced wife

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum financial provision (muta') for a divorced woman if the husband is poor?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) elucidates the practical application of Quranic verse 2:241, defining the minimum 'matāʿ' (gracious provision) for a financially constrained (muʿsir) husband as a simple headscarf or similar modest item. This interpretation highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on flexibility and ease in marital obligations, ensuring that financial hardship does not negate the husband's duty to provide a token of goodwill and dignity to his divorced wife.
